correctness.rationale: For every real unit u and theta>0, the normalized one-step Rayleigh quotient is exact. The four-sign product depends only on q=sum pairwise u_i^2 u_j^2 and r=product u_i^2, with verified polynomial identity. At q<=1/4 it is bounded below uniquely by the equal two-support case. At q>1/4 fixed-q minimization of r forces two equal larger squares; the reduced one-parameter derivative has no interior minimum and hence only equal-two/equal-three endpoints survive. An exact crossing polynomial gives theta*=5 sqrt(10)-14. Jensen gives the unique coordinate-axis maximum and strictly positive logdet bias. Exact symbolic/rational verifier replay passed 45867 checks; finite checks are not used as infinite proof.

Novelty is qualified by a genuine precedence risk for unlocated extremal logarithmic Rademacher-sum literature.

value.rationale: The one-node stochastic Lanczos logdet approximation is a concrete well-motivated low-matrix-vector-product regime. For a fixed 3x3 rank-one spectral family, the exact expected bias changes its most favorable Rademacher eigenbasis orientation at a nontrivial algebraic spike threshold. This gives a complete orientation-sensitive benchmark, unique equality cases and a warning that same-spectrum eigenvalue-only bounds conceal probe distribution dependence. Three coordinates are minimal to express a genuine two-versus-three nonzero-support competition. The result is not a textbook Jensen inequality alone, a random slice, or a claim of practical superiority over two-node quadrature.
